title: Annotatio IV §.III from Prior (1): Stretch any error into heresy, or lesser dissent into fundamental
pass_a_gloss: From the Prior (1.) To turn any Error into heresy at will, or a dissent of lesser moment into a fundamental one; into a fundamental one, I say, when the dissent is either entirely feigned and so none, or only Verbal, or at most concerns the Mode of the thing.
pass_b_english: From the first fountain: (1.) Stretch any error into heresy at will, or turn a lesser dissent into a fundamental one.
“Fundamental,” I mean, when the dissent is wholly feigned and so none at all, or only verbal, or at most about the mode of the thing.
source_text: Ex Priori (1.) Errorem quemvis, in haeresin pro libidine vertere, vel dissensum minoris momenti, in fundamentalem; In fundamentalem, inquam, quando vel omnino fictus est dissensus eoque nullus, vel Verbalis tantùm, vel ad summum, Modum rei concernens.
